A new milestone has been reached in the open source AI space. Open models from China are now outperforming recently released competitors, such as Opus 4.8, just two months after their debut.

Kimi K3, now holding the top spot among open weights models at 57 in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, has made its weights publicly available. The 2.6T parameter model, released under the 'Kimi K3 License,' is labeled as 'Commercial Use Restricted.'

This licensing means businesses offering model-as-a-service solutions with over $20 million in annual revenue must seek additional agreements. Products exceeding 100 million monthly active users or generating $20 million in monthly revenue must clearly display "Kimi K3" in their user interface.

A technical report outlining the model's architecture and training methods has also been released.

🤖 Anthropic launches free Claude Code course

Anthropic released a free course showing real scenarios of Claude Code in action. It teaches how to turn Claude Code into a full AI agent that writes code, works with GitHub, automates routine tasks, uses hooks and skills, and handles long tasks with minimal human control.

The course has about 15 short lessons and ends with a certificate. It aims to help developers quickly master Claude Code and use it effectively.

OpenAI research shows that 43.5% of occupation-specific ChatGPT messages from U.S. business users related to tasks typically handled by a different profession. This indicates users are leveraging the model to address specialist work outside their primary field.

Financial calculations and computer troubleshooting were among the top three most common tasks handled beyond users’ professions in all groups. Marketing-related tasks also appeared frequently across various occupations.

The data captured messages within ChatGPT Business, not finished work, so it does not measure quality, productivity, or impact on jobs.

Researchers note that, especially in small businesses, employees often solve problems outside their usual roles. AI is emerging as a versatile support tool across different functions.

🤖 Anthropic explains why it still won’t release frontier open-weight AI models

While much of the AI industry is rallying behind open-weight models, Anthropic is holding its ground.

The company says today’s most powerful AI systems are becoming capable enough that releasing their weights could make it much easier for bad actors to build dangerous cyber, biological, or autonomous attack tools. Instead of full public releases, Anthropic argues for controlled access through APIs, where safety measures can be monitored and updated.

At the same time, Anthropic says it isn’t against open-weight AI. It supports open research and believes open-weight models have an important role in innovation. The company says it may release open-weight models in the future but only when they can be deployed with what it considers adequate safety protections.

🤖 OpenAI adds Health mode to ChatGPT

OpenAI’s Health mode lets ChatGPT access your medical records and Apple Watch data to answer health questions with real metrics. Users link Apple Health and records from One Medical or Function Health to share tests, medications, visits, sleep, and activity.

ChatGPT compares blood tests, explains medical terms, or suggests allergy-safe restaurants. Around 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions weekly, with 70% starting outside medical sections, so context now flows in regular chats.

Free users get GPT-5.5 Instant, which flags when a live doctor is needed. Paid users access GPT-5.6 Sol, better at complex cases and explanations.
